verdict.line: You lose if you let Sett close distance and trade autos into his Q (Knuckle Down) stacks; you win if you hold Cannon form and poke him down before he's forced to commit.

brief.thesis: Jayce in Cannon stance outranges Sett's entire kit (his longest engage, E (Facebreaker), only reaches 490), so this matchup is a straightforward kiting check that measures at 49.3% over 209 games. The catch is Sett's passive, Pit Grit, regenerates health the lower he drops, so single pokes don't close him out — you need sustained Q (Shock Blast) chip, not one big burst, or he just sustains back to even.

theirWindow.when: He lands first Q (Knuckle Down) hit
theirWindow.what: Knuckle Down empowers his next two attacks with bonus max-health damage on cooldown 9/8/7/6/5s — back off immediately after the first empowered hit lands instead of trading into the second.

yourWindow.when: E (Acceleration Gate) is up and he's not in melee range
yourWindow.what: Fire Q (Shock Blast) through your own E (Acceleration Gate) to get the boosted missile speed, range, and damage, then follow with W (Lightning Field) procs while kiting — this is your highest-value poke window.

start.why: 92.7% pick rate at 49.6% win rate over 252 games — the sustain and early AD let you trade autos in Cannon stance without losing the lane-sustain war to his passive regen.

boots.why: 53.1% win rate over 96 games — Sett's entire kit is auto-attack and physical-damage based, so the flat reduction blunts his empowered Knuckle Down hits more than Lucidity's cooldowns do here.

runes.keystoneWhy: 51.4% win rate over the recorded sample — Conqueror's healing directly counters the sustain-check nature of this lane (OP.GG's own tip is to damage him often), letting your stacked poke out-heal his passive Grit regen.

summoners.why: Highest measured win rate at 55.4% and the most-picked combo (49.6%) — Teleport lets you reset after poke-only exchanges without losing wave or tower pressure, which fits a lane where you aren't forced to all-in.

playing.title: Default to Cannon stance
playing.detail: Stay in Cannon form and poke with Q (Shock Blast) at its 600 range rather than swapping to Hammer form to melee trade — his entire kit requires him to close distance first.

playing.title: Punish the first Knuckle Down hit
playing.detail: His Q (Knuckle Down) empowers his next two attacks with max-health damage on a 9/8/7/6/5s cooldown — disengage after the first empowered hit connects instead of eating the second.

playing.title: Remember Facebreaker needs two sides
playing.detail: E (Facebreaker) only stuns if enemies are on opposite sides of him; alone in a 1v1 you'll just be slowed, not stunned, unless an ally is on his far side.

playing.title: Don't duel through his W shield
playing.detail: Haymaker converts stored damage-taken into a shield plus true damage at center / physical damage on the sides — if he casts it while you're fighting, step off-center to eat the lesser physical split, not the true damage.

playing.title: Chain Shock Blast through Acceleration Gate
playing.detail: Deploy E (Acceleration Gate) and fire Q (Shock Blast) through it for boosted missile speed, range, and damage — this is your safest way to apply the sustained chip his passive sustain requires.

playing.title: Respect his ultimate from level 6
playing.detail: R (The Show Stopper) has a long 120/100/80/80/80s cooldown but only needs 400 range to drag and slam you — don't overextend on a poke read right after he's used Q or E to close distance.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and all win-rate/pick-rate figures are pulled directly from measured OP.GG games on the current patch; the ability mechanics, trade timings, and tactical reasoning are my own analysis layered on top of that data.
